clue.text: It requires a truly consistent performance from its cast

definitions.text: It requires a truly consistent performance from its cast

parts.note: surface reading: an actor who never has an off night; setter's reading: the acting must be consistent with the truth, re-enacting real events

explanation.surface: A director demands that every actor holds their standard night after night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truly consistent' seems to mean reliable, but it means faithful to what really happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a dramatised film of real events, so its actors must stay true to the facts.

clue.text: Renaissance artist's Doctor Swallowing Midge

indicators.note: whatever swallows something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation for doctor
Midge Ure, the Scottish singer of Ultravox

explanation.surface: A painter's physician swallows a small biting insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Midge looks like the insect but is the first name of the musician, so only his surname enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the leading German painter and engraver of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Scrapped lunch to take north-eastern link to the continent

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up, so its letters are free to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A cancelled lunch makes way for a trip to the Continent from the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chunnel is the informal name for the Channel Tunnel, the rail tunnel joining Britain to France.

clue.text: The end of the said potty is missing

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the remaining letters go into a mad new order
the word is is missing, so those letters drop out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
these letters are removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A garbled riddle about the end of an aforementioned chamber pot going missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip I and S from THE SAID to leave THEAD, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is the end of life, so 'the end' is a common euphemism for it.

clue.text: Same sad converts got together

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters are re-formed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The same gloomy religious converts gathered as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or gather into a heap, so amassed matches got together.

clue.text: A programmer's A-Z?

parts.note: surface reading: a street atlas or reference guide a coder might carry; setter's reading: the routine that puts a list into order from A to Z

explanation.walkthrough: A-Z is the British name for a street-map book, but here it means arranging items from first letter to last.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphasort is a computing operation arranging records in alphabetical sequence, from A through to Z.

clue.text: Finish filming western with pop music

parts.note: standard abbreviation for west or western
rap is a genre of popular music

explanation.surface: A film crew finishes shooting a cowboy picture with a pop soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: In film-making, to wrap a shoot is to complete it, as in 'that's a wrap'.

clue.text: Young predator put away — copper goes by book

indicators.note: one thing going by another sits right beside it, so the pieces are placed next to each other

parts.note: to wolf food is to put it away greedily
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A youngster is locked away while a policeman goes strictly by the rulebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal's symbol; 'put away' means eaten, not jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf cub is a baby wolf, and the wolf is a hunting animal.

clue.text: Putting a lid on piano, celebrated vocalist demonstrates one way to sing

indicators.note: putting one thing on another stacks it on top, so in a down entry it comes before

parts.note: taken as written
a cap is a lid, as on a bottle
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
Ella Fitzgerald, the famous jazz singer

explanation.surface: A singer closes the piano lid and shows how to perform unaccompanied.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is done by voices alone, with no instrumental accompaniment.

clue.text: Book about our deceptive barrier causes fuss

parts.note: standard abbreviation for book

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or in a different order, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a ha-ha is a sunken ditch acting as a hidden fence in a landscaped park

explanation.surface: A book about a misleading fence on our estate stirs up a row.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a ditch with a wall in it, used on English country estates so the boundary cannot be seen from the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or overexcited reaction, the same thing as a fuss.

clue.text: From casual perusal, telescope finally picked out a star

indicators.note: a casual reading is loose and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
something picked out of a whole is taken away from it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of telescope

explanation.surface: An astronomer idly scanning the sky through a telescope spots a star.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from PERUSAL to leave PRUSAL, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulsar is a rapidly spinning neutron star that emits regular pulses of radiation.

clue.text: Food chain: bear comes first, though not invariably top

indicators.note: this fixes the order, putting the animal ahead of the other piece
not tells us to do without the letter just identified

parts.note: Bruin is a traditional name for a bear

indicators.note: the top of a word written across is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of invariably, to be removed
ch is the abbreviation for a chain, an old unit of length

explanation.surface: In a food chain the bear ranks first, though it is not always the top predator.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from BRUIN, then add CH; 'food chain' is a false phrase, as 'Food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Oil perhaps to be seen from ocean liner?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: oil leaked into the water, visible from a ship

definitions.text: to be seen from ocean liner
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: an oil painting of the view a passenger has out at sea

explanation.walkthrough: Oil suggests a slick on the water, but it is an oil painting; the scene is what a ship's passenger looks at.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a picture of the sea, often painted in oils, showing the view across open water.

clue.text: Dramatic family union abandoned? Here's a pill!

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: the Capulets are Juliet's family in Romeo and Juliet
standard abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: A theatrical family's marriage falls apart, so someone reaches for medication.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing U from CAPULET leaves the answer; the abandoned union also nods to Romeo and Juliet's doomed marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A caplet is a smooth, oval-shaped coated tablet, a type of pill.

clue.text: Formerly, formerly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: previously, in times past
second sense: a word used in former times, labelled archaic

explanation.walkthrough: The repetition is the joke: the answer means 'formerly' and is itself a word from former days.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforetime is an archaic adverb meaning previously or in earlier times.

clue.text: Entertainer Chuck plus reindeer

parts.note: to chuck someone under the chin is to give a light tap
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A performer named Chuck takes the stage alongside a reindeer.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck looks like a name or a verb meaning throw, but here it means a gentle pat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap dancer performs rhythmic dancing in metal-tipped shoes, a stage entertainer.

clue.text: When depressed, you could find it helps to get over the threshold

definitions.text: When depressed, you could find it helps to get over the threshold

parts.words: When depressed, you could find it helps to get over the threshold
parts.note: surface reading: someone feeling low who needs help to move on; setter's reading: a button that, when pressed, gets a visitor let in at the front entrance

explanation.walkthrough: Depressed means pushed down, and the threshold is a literal doorstep, not a mental barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the button at a house entrance rings to summon the occupant, who lets you in.

clue.text: Hairgrip made of copper with reverse catch

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer, like a copper

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the next word's letters from end to start

parts.note: to nip is to catch or pinch

explanation.surface: A hair clip made from copper metal with a back-facing clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobby pin is the American name for a sprung hairgrip that holds hair in place.

clue.text: Music culture movement responsible for bad trip during dance

indicators.note: one event during another happens inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a bop is an informal dance

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoiled, so the word's letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A youth music scene is blamed for someone's bad drug experience at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Britpop was the 1990s British guitar-band scene of Oasis and Blur.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was a 1990s musical and cultural movement centred on British guitar bands.

clue.text: Avoid 'en' shaped like a birthmark

indicators.note: shaped means given a new form, so the letters are moulded into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning to steer clear of them, the ones marked with a birthmark-like shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaped like' reads as one phrase, but 'shaped' is the anagram signal and 'like a birthmark' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A naevus is a birthmark or mole, and naevoid is the adjective meaning resembling one.

clue.text: Head driller and surrogate parent

indicators.note: a surrogate is a substitute, so the word is replaced by a version of its own letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chief engineer at an oil rig who is also a surrogate mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: Head driller suggests a foreman at a drilling site, but it is a surgical tool that bores into the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a cylindrical saw used by surgeons to cut a hole in the skull.

clue.text: Are in conflict with USA over one geographical area

indicators.note: things in conflict are thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Nations fight with America over a single disputed region.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, a large region of the globe.

clue.text: Iced preparation used in horse health scheme

indicators.note: used in places the treated word inside the next piece

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: a preparation is something made up, so the letters are made up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A cold ointment is applied as part of an equine health plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicare is the US federal health insurance programme for older people.

clue.text: Hardline leader breaks up rubbish party

indicators.note: breaking up a word splits it open so another letter can go inside

parts.note: trash means rubbish

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Hardline

explanation.surface: A strict leader shuts down a disreputable gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish party' reads as a dull party, but 'party' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: In effect, we ensure bard's in the middle

indicators.note: In says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: In practice, we make sure Shakespeare stays at the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The bard is Shakespeare, who uses the shortened 'tween for between.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Tween is a poetic contraction of between, meaning in the middle, as used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Seconds before bird's sudden dash

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: standard abbreviation for seconds
a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: Moments before a bird suddenly darts off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoot is a quick run or rush, so it can serve as a noun for a sudden dash.

clue.text: Life of a celebrity that's been shot

definitions.text: Life of a celebrity that's been shot

parts.words: Life of a celebrity that's been shot
parts.note: surface reading: a famous person killed by gunfire; setter's reading: a life story that has been filmed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests an assassination, but it means filmed on camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film telling the life story of a real, often famous, person.

clue.text: After a number of deliveries, he collects ball for Oxford defender?

indicators.note: After puts the following material behind the first piece

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like a round ball

explanation.surface: A cricketer catches the ball after several overs and defends for Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university team, but it is an oxford, a laced leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An overshoe is worn over an ordinary shoe, such as an oxford, to protect it from wet and dirt.

clue.text: Horn sound in live recording

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A horn blast captured on a live album.
explanation.definitionFit: A car horn makes a short, high-pitched beep.

clue.text: Suspect ranted about Brown being dismissed?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged word goes round the colour
suspect means dubious or not right, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A suspected protester raged about Gordon Brown being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'dismissed' is a sense of losing your job rather than a direct synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers made redundant in Britain are laid off because their job no longer exists.
